dedupe_keys.name: gemstat global freshwater quality database of the unep gems water programme

description: GEMStat is the global inland water quality database of the United Nations Environment Programme's GEMS/Water Programme, a monitoring network founded in 1978, and is hosted by the GEMS/Water Data Centre in Koblenz, Germany. Coverage: as of January 2026 more than 61 million entries from monitoring stations in more than 90 countries, mostly rivers, then groundwater and lakes, with the densest coverage in Europe and Latin America and the Caribbean; samples span 1906 to 2023, with 2024 and 2025 samples from a few countries such as Belgium, Japan, the Netherlands and the Republic of Korea; more than 600 parameters classified by the CUAHSI Hydrosphere Ontology, mostly chemical (organic compounds, inorganics, nutrients), then physical and a few biological. Format and access: a data portal for station, country or catchment selection, statistics and charts, a custom data request form, and an annual direct download on Zenodo (doi:10.5281/zenodo.13881899) of the data shared under CC BY 4.0 or an equivalent open licence; a parameter catalogue in XLSX. Licence: CC BY 4.0 or equivalent for the openly shared part; other data follow the provider's terms through the request route. Caveats: on 28 September 2026 the site announced that data downloads were out of order and asked users to request data by contact; the station count on the availability page is misprinted (31,0000), so the exact number was not confirmed; the Zenodo record was not opened. Simulation uses: raw water quality baselines for drinking water treatment, wastewater discharge and catchment models in capacity planning and climate adaptation. Related records: WISE Freshwater (data-eea-wise-freshwater-information-system) for European water body status.
